item.title: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures
item.description:
Pontiff tells Argentina’s president the economy must benefit all on second stop of 12-day Latin America tour Pope Leo XIV has delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s harsh austerity measures, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires. “The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy,” he said on Sunday, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour. item.title: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner as Germany’s first woman president
item.description:
Crystalyne Curley is set to become the first woman president of the Navajo Nation, the largest reservation by land mass in the country. Curley, who also held the distinction of being the first woman to serve as the Nation’s council speaker — the head of its legislative branch —when she was voted by council members to fill that role in 2023, has worked on issues related to water rights, uranium contamination and voter rights. In another first for tribal governments, the Seneca Nation of Indians in New York also elected its first woman president, Tina Abrams. She previously served two terms on the Nation’s council. While Native women made history for their tribes in this election, it is not uncommon for women to hold top positions in tribal nations. item.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot begins the hard work of forging a coalition government
item.description:
Israel’s president tapped Gadi Eisenkot to try to form the country’s next government, kicking off a tortuous negotiating process that could oust long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. While Eisenkot and Netanyahu differ in style and substance , both men reflect the “ monolithically anti-Palestinian stance that dominates Israeli politics,” an International Crisis Group expert told Le Monde. There is also little “real difference” between the two on Iran, an Israeli analyst said, though recent elections in the US and Israel have created further uncertainty around the simmering conflict: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that further US strikes were “ highly unlikely ,” while Iran — which has taken credit for Republicans’ poor midterm showing — said negotiations were paused following the “shock” election result. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Pope tells Argentina’s Milei leaders should know limits of power
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday from Uruguay, where his Latin America tour began, facing calls to help bridge divisions after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei. The visit to Buenos Aires is the first by a pontiff to the late Pope Francis’s homeland in nearly four decades.

item.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
item.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. item.title: How a bank collapse left millions in limbo and toppled Paraguay's president
item.description:
Paraguay’s president was removed from office and detained after the country’s largest digital bank melted down, leaving half the populace without access to funds and plunging the country into a political crisis. A youth-friendly banking app, Ueno collapsed amid allegations of insider lending and proximity to the country’s longtime ruling party, which is closely aligned with Washington. The app was credited with expanding access in a region where as many as one in four adults does not have a bank account ; its implosion was a “ kind of tsunami in the end ,” a political scientist said, and puts at stake “the credibility of a country that has spent years trying to establish itself as a stable , reliable destination for international investment,” a regional analyst wrote in Americas Quarterly. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers worst-ever local elections result
item.description:
Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party . Continue reading...

item.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean
item.description:
Wolfgang Kaehler / Wolfgang Kaehler, Getty Images Two fishermen rescued a Royal Caribbean cruise ship pianist nearly 20 miles off Newport Beach in the Pacific Ocean. The man was treading water and is believed to have been stranded at sea for about nine hours before they found him. “I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” one of the fishermen, Grant Garrett, was quoted telling CBS News. “Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up,” Sean Norton said. “He was in total shock.” The man, whose identity has not been revealed, was hospitalized and is expected to survive. “The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton recalled. item.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
item.description:
US, Russian, and Ukrainian officials are expected to meet this week in Abu Dhabi for talks on ending the nearly five-year war, but experts cautioned that the meetings were unlikely to yield a major breakthrough. The first direct negotiations in nine months will address “ security guarantees for Ukraine , Europe’s post-war security architecture and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction,” envoy Steve Witkoff said; Washington’s efforts to end the war have been primarily focused on rebuilding commercial ties , though earlier efforts surrounding a potential Alaskan LNG terminal collapsed in response to what US investors described as secret Russian control . “As long as the White House is satisfied with small gestures rather than actual concessions, Putin will not reverse course ,” an Atlantic Council expert wrote. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Native American women made history in tribal, state and federal elections
item.description:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women. On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT . item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes leave hundreds of thousands without power
item.description:
Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without electricity on Sunday following Russian airstrikes targeting the country's energy infrastructure. Moscow has intensified its attacks as winter approaches, leaving residents in Kyiv and other parts of the country struggling with power cuts as temperatures continue to drop. Clemence Waller reports.

item.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
item.description:
National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc. On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties. item.title: Mourning in Poland after mass shooting
item.description:
Poland has launched a terrorism investigation after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 16 injured. The 24-year-old Polish suspect was reportedly fascinated by far-right ideologies. Authorities are investigating the possible extremist motive as Krakow's main square remains sealed. Two days of national mourning have been declared for the victims.

item.title: G7 ministers meet as Europe seeks greater say in Ukraine peace talks
item.description:
G7 foreign ministers will revisit Russia’s war in Ukraine and the prospect of further US strikes on Iran when they meet in Paris on Monday. Washington has kept the option of new strikes open since Republicans lost the midterm elections. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is due to attend both days, unlike the March meeting where he only came for one.
